headline: S&P PUTS NVIDIA ON
dek: The ratings agency says Jensen Huang’s departure and reinstatement don’t answer its questions about how Nvidia’s board oversees its CEO.

ladder.note: NVIDIA TODAY · now on CreditWatch Negative
POSSIBLE · S&P expects any cut limited to one notch

graphic.ladder_note: Bigger cut possible only if investigations or disclosures hurt Nvidia’s reputation or business, S&P says.

flags.title: BOARD OVERSIGHT
flags.text: The CEO’s “departure, then reinstatement … does not sufficiently answer our questions regarding board oversight of executive code of conduct.”

flags.title: BOARD INDEPENDENCE
flags.text: “The long tenure of certain board members may have compromised their independence.”

flags.title: SUCCESSION
flags.text: “Weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” put “key man” risk up front. Huang told staff Tuesday Nvidia doesn’t need a succession plan, per CNBC.

flags.title: CHINA & EXPORTS
flags.text: China exposure raises questions on “geopolitical risk management and internal controls.”

steps.text: S&P places Nvidia on CreditWatch Negative
S&P plans to meet Nvidia’s board and management
Huang due before House panels and Senate Banking

means.label: Not a downgrade yet:
means.text: Nvidia keeps its AA rating for now. S&P says the company’s competitive position, technology lead and financial profile are “unchanged at this time.”

means.label: Nvidia’s side:
means.text: On Nov. 17 the board created a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. S&P says it’s unaware of any board remedy for the governance gaps it flagged.

means.label: Not cited:
means.text: S&P’s note doesn’t mention the administration’s role in Huang’s return. It points to the CEO news and export-control questions.

sources: Sources: S&P Global Ratings research update, Nov. 25, 2026; Reuters, Nov. 25; CNBC, Nov. 24; Nvidia press release, Nov. 17; NBC News, Nov. 24. Rating scale shown is S&P’s top four long-term grades.
